subject: Order Form: staggered commit slicing and tax / surcharge treatment
body:
--- Message 1 (2025-03-11 09:14 PDT) ---
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@stellum.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: payments@stellum.com
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Stellum order form questions — commit phasing and tax treatment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement had a quick pass at the Order Form and flagged two areas we need clarified before Legal will accept:

1) Minimum commit phasing: your OF currently lists a 12-month $360k minimum with quarterly tranche invoicing. We need to confirm whether unused tokens in an early tranche can be applied to later tranches (we prefer a rolling pool) or if they expire at tranche boundary.

2) Tax & surcharge treatment: in our country we have a standard 5% digital services surcharge that our AP team expects to pay on gross invoice amount unless the vendor confirms reverse charge or VAT equivalence. Can you confirm Redwood's position on passing through any local surcharges vs netting into the upfront credit?

I've attached the draft OF and our tax certificate for your review. Can you loop in commercial/legal and let us know proposed language for the tranche expiry and a short line for the tax appendix that our procurement can sign off on?

Best,
Marta
Marta Gomez
Head of Procurement — Stellum Analytics
body_reply_1:
--- Message 2 (2025-03-11 10:42 PDT) ---
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@stellum.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, payments@stellum.com
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 10:42:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stellum order form questions — commit phasing and tax treatment

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear notes and for sharing the tax cert. Quick answers up front, and then next steps: 

- Tranche usage: we can do a single rolling pool across the 12-month period (i.e., unused tokens from Q1 can be used in Q2/Q3), but we need to reflect that in the Order Form language and adjust invoicing memo for visibility.
- Surcharges: Redwood's standard approach is to pass through statutory, customer-specific surcharges if they're an explicit, local statutory obligation (we've handled this as a pass-through in EMEA/LatAm contracts). However, we can offer an alternative where the surcharge is absorbed into the prepay and we reduce the upfront invoice amount accordingly — that requires approval from Finance for the netting treatment.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) I'm attaching a redline (orderform_redlines_kp.docx) with: a) a clause to convert tranches to a rolling-pool; b) optional tax appendix language with two variants (pass-through vs netted).
2) Ben / Karthik — can you review the netting option and confirm whether Finance would accept absorbing the 5% for this deal if Stellum signs a 12-month firm commit?
3) Marta / Stellum AP — if pass-through is required, please confirm if the surcharge is statutory and point us to the local guidance.

I'll follow up after I get finance's call.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
body_internal_discussion:
--- Message 3 (2025-03-11 13:05 PDT) ---
From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Stellum order form questions — internal finance check

Kim / Karthik / Lauren — quick internal. If Finance absorbs the 5% surcharge for the 12-month commit it costs us roughly $18k (5% of $360k). Two considerations:
- Commercial: absorbing helps remove friction and speeds EAA execution.
- Precedent: absorbing may set a precedent for other EU/LatAm enterprise deals; we should gate on either (a) signing a multi-year or (b) a booking/QBR exception.

Suggested compromise: offer netting (absorb surcharge) as a one-time concession for DEAL-7821 in return for an explicit clause: customer will not seek surcharge credits or retro requests for other accounts and add a one-time credit runbook item into the Order Form. Also add a clause that if surcharge exceeds 7% we revert to pass-through.

Lauren — can you confirm cashflow impact and whether accounting needs any special handling on invoice templates? Also flag any G/L mapping issues if we net vs pass-through.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 13 Mar 2025 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Stellum order form questions — commit phasing and tax treatment

Hi Marta — quick update following internal review:

- Rolling pool: confirmed. We've updated the OF redline to read: 
  "All prepaid units/credits purchased under this Order Form shall be available as a single rolling pool for the Term; unused units shall not expire while the Term remains in effect."

- Surcharge: Finance has approved a one-time netting concession for DEAL-7821. The proposed contract appendix (attached) includes two short paragraphs: one describing the pass-through option, and the second (the operative clause for this deal) confirming Redwood will net the 5% surcharge from the upfront invoice and absorb the amount as a one-time concession, subject to a maximum of 7% in any single invoice.

Practical items:
- If Stellum accepts the netting concession we will issue the invoice for the net amount next week. Please confirm whether PO routing expects the gross figure to appear on the PO (we can include a memo line showing the gross and the concession amount).
- We've attached the redlined OF and the proposed tax appendix (20250311_Stellum_OrderForm_draft.pdf, orderform_redlines_kp.docx).

If that sounds good I can push the updated OF into DocuSign and loop legal for the final MSA cross-ref.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
